title: Palworld Best Mounts Guide | Ground, Water and Flying Pals Ranked | Palworld Guide
description: A Palworld 1.0 mount guide: how saddles work, the best early ground, water and flying mounts, why Jetragon is the fastest flyer, the late game ground picks and the speed passives that stack.

sections.heading: Why mounts matter
sections.script: Palworld is a huge map, and walking across it gets old fast. A good mount saves you time, carries you over water, and lets you fight while you move. In this guide we cover how saddles work, the best early mounts on the ground, on water and in the air, the mid game upgrades, the fastest flyer in the game, the late game ground kings, and the speed passives that make any mount quicker. One note before we start. Mount guides do not agree on every number, and Palworld changed in version one point zero, so we will only state what several sources agree on. Check the technology menu in your own game for exact levels. Ready to ride? Let us start with the basics. We will go terrain by terrain, from the cheap early rides to the legendary speed kings, so you can pick the right mount for where you are in the game right now.

sections.heading: How saddles work
sections.script: Every mount follows the same simple steps. First you unlock the saddle for that Pal in the technology menu. Then you craft the saddle. Then you place the Pal in your party, and finally you mount it. Guides agree on this routine. Once you are riding, you can use the Pal's partner skill, and that is where mounts get interesting. Some let you cross water, some jump higher, and some fire missiles. Mounts also keep their normal job. A Pal that works at your base can still be a fine ride when you leave. Early saddles are cheap to make, so you can add a mount very early in a run. Later saddles cost more, and the best ones unlock at high technology levels, so plan your technology points with your mount goals in mind. A mount also saves your own stamina, which matters on long trips.

sections.heading: Your first ground mount
sections.script: On the ground, the most recommended early mount is Direhowl. Two guides put its saddle at about level nine, which is the earliest saddle on one list and makes it the classic first ride. Direhowl is a Neutral Pal, it is fast for its stage, and it is easy to find before you reach any legendary Pals. Its partner skill lets you ride it as a proper mount. For most players, Direhowl is the one to build first, and it stays useful until you reach the mid game. Let us move on to water.

sections.heading: Crossing the water
sections.script: Water mounts are optional, but they open up the coast and the islands. The earliest choice is Surfent, a Water Pal whose saddle unlocks at a low level, around ten to sixteen depending on the guide. Its partner skill lets you glide across the surface safely, which is perfect for the first lakes and short sea trips. Later on, Jormuntide is the endgame option. Two guides place its saddle at around level forty, and it is both a strong swimmer and a strong fighter, since it is a Dragon and Water Pal. Neptilius is the other name you will see. Several guides call it the fastest swimmer in the game, with a leap that carries you high out of the water. A small tip, if you ride in the sea, keep an eye on your stamina and the Pals nearby.

sections.heading: First wings: Nitewing and Vanwyrm
sections.script: Flying changes everything. You skip mountains, cross rivers, and spot Alpha Pals from above. For most players the first flyer is Nitewing. Two guides call it the first flying mount most players reach, and the usual first set of wings. Nitewing is not the fastest, but it is easy to get. The next step up is Vanwyrm, which guides describe as an easy speed upgrade for the mid game. Neither one needs rare materials. If you want to explore the sky early and cheaply, these two are the answer. After that, the big upgrades arrive.

sections.heading: Mid game flyers
sections.script: Between the starter wings and the legendaries, a group of strong flyers sits in the middle. Guides repeatedly name Beakon and Ragnahawk as the upgrades before the endgame. Both are noticeably faster than Nitewing, and both are far easier to reach than a legendary. Then comes Frostallion. Two guides call it the best flying mount short of Jetragon. It is a strong fighter as well as a fast ride, and its Dark variant, Frostallion Noct, is rated just as highly. If you are going for a mid game flying team, this group is a safe bet.

sections.heading: Jetragon, the speed king
sections.script: Now the star of the list. Jetragon is the fastest mount in Palworld, according to several guides, with a sprint speed of about three thousand three hundred. That is more than double Frostallion. While you ride it, its Aerial Missile partner skill fires homing projectiles, so you can attack as you fly. The catch is that you have to find and catch it first, since it is a late game legendary. We covered legendary locations in other guides. If you want to cross the map in a blink, this is the Pal to chase.

sections.heading: Late game ground kings
sections.script: The ground has its own endgame. Here the guides disagree, so we will be careful. Several guides name Necromus as the ground king, with Paladius close behind, and one list gives them sprint speeds of about nineteen hundred and eighteen hundred. Both dash forward with their attacks while you ride. Both are legendary Pals. Another mount guide instead names Hartalis as the best ground mount, and a second guide ties it with Necromus at around nineteen hundred. Hartalis is a raid boss Pal, so you have to defeat it before you can ride it. So the safe answer is that Necromus and Hartalis are the fastest on land, and Paladius is close. All three are worth the trouble.

sections.heading: Speed passives that stack
sections.script: Your mount can go even faster with the right passives. Four of them matter for movement. Swift adds thirty percent movement speed, Runner adds twenty percent, Legend adds fifteen percent with extra attack and defense, and Nimble adds ten percent. Guides agree on these numbers, and they say the bonuses stack, so a Pal with Swift and Runner gets fifty percent. Legendary Pals such as Jetragon and Frostallion come with Legend built in. If you breed your own mount, aim for Swift and Runner on the same Pal. That can turn a mid game mount into something that rivals a legendary. Remember that each passive can only appear once on a Pal, so the best you can stack from these four is a very large bonus.

sections.heading: Your mount plan
sections.script: Here is a simple plan. Early, build Direhowl for the ground and Surfent for the water. Soon after, add Nitewing and then Vanwyrm for the sky. In the mid game, move up to Beakon, Ragnahawk or Frostallion. Late, chase Jetragon in the air, and Necromus, Paladius or Hartalis on the ground, with Jormuntide or Neptilius for the sea. Then add Swift and Runner by breeding. That covers every terrain, and you never need to walk across the map again. Keep in mind that you do not need every mount on this list. One good ground mount, one flyer and one swimmer are enough for most players. Which mount is your favorite, and which one are you still hunting?
